title.zh: 镜像对称等离子体 Green 磁通矩阵

summary: Build the dense flux-response matrix for a uniformly spaced, Z-reflection-symmetric cylindrical grid.

capability: Build the dense flux-response matrix for a uniformly spaced, Z-reflection-symmetric cylindrical grid.
operation: symmetric R-Z grid -> target-row/source-column flux response
discovery.model: Axisymmetric ideal circular-filament flux with symmetry-required grid validation.
discovery.geometry: Rectilinear R-Z grid shared by target and source nodes.
discovery.boundary: R is nonnegative and increasing; Z is increasing, uniform and symmetric about zero; axis-source columns and self entries are zero.

identity.direction: symmetric R,Z grid to target-row/source-column psi response
identity.definition: Use actual-coordinate circular-filament flux entries on the supplied grid and preserve C-order flattening.
identity.model: Axisymmetric ideal circular-filament flux with symmetry-required grid validation.
identity.geometry: Rectilinear R-Z grid shared by target and source nodes.
identity.coordinates: R,Z in metres; matrix entries Wb/rad/A.
identity.boundary: R is nonnegative and increasing; Z is increasing, uniform, and symmetric about zero; axis-source columns and self entries are zero.
assumptions: The input grid is finite and matching.
The source grid has at least two nodes per axis.
No cell-area or 2pi factor is included.

inputs.name: r_grid
inputs.description: Cylindrical radius mesh shared by source and target cells.
inputs.constraints: Finite, rectilinear, nonnegative and strictly increasing R axis; same shape as z_grid and at least two points per axis.

inputs.name: z_grid
inputs.description: Axial coordinate mesh shared by source and target cells.
inputs.constraints: Finite rectilinear grid with a strictly increasing, uniformly spaced and reflection-symmetric Z axis; same shape as r_grid and at least two points per axis.

outputs.name: g_psi
outputs.description: Psi=R A_phi response per source current for each target/source grid-cell pair.
outputs.constraints: Both axes follow C-order [Z,R] flattening; axis-source columns and nonfinite formula elements use the zero convention; no cell-area or 2*pi factor is included.

preconditions: The input grid is finite and matching.
The source grid has at least two nodes per axis.
supported: Symmetric-grid shape/finiteness, axis-source convention, reflected blocks, and direct-kernel comparison.
excluded: Nonsymmetric grids, finite-wire self-fields, and arbitrary physical plasma qualification.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError is raised for malformed, nonfinite, nonrectilinear, nonuniform, or nonsymmetric grids.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: FloatingPointError from an unrepresentable Green matrix propagates.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; matrix construction is direct.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No matrix mapping is returned after validation or kernel failure.

example.description: Build a 3x4 reflection-symmetric grid response matrix.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import build_mirror_plasma_flux_green
r_grid, z_grid = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(0.0, 0.3, 4), np.linspace(-0.4, 0.4, 3))
g_psi = build_mirror_plasma_flux_green(r_grid, z_grid)['g_psi']
assert g_psi.shape == (r_grid.size, r_grid.size)
assert np.isfinite(g_psi).all()
for source_plane in range(3):
    np.testing.assert_allclose(g_psi[:, source_plane*4], 0.0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(g_psi[0:4, 4:8], g_psi[4:8, 0:4])
example.expected: The result is a finite float64 (12,12) matrix with zero axis-source columns and equal reflected blocks.

scope: The first source plane is compared column by column with an independent 80-digit elliptic-integral expression; the original binary64 checker cancellation was proven by independent high precision and repaired, and the rtol=2e-14 gate is retained.
Whole-matrix equality with direct dense filament columns on a symmetric grid.
Square shape, finite output and axis-source zero-column convention.
Rejection of an axially nonsymmetric grid and reflection-block relation.

Independent 70/80-digit ideal-loop relation checks cover very small positive radii, near-axis nonzero BR, near-wire cases and formula-evaluation branches while retaining the original numeric assertions and tolerances; the exact self term and arithmetic failure are handled separately.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct SciRel tests establish selected source-plane formula values, whole-matrix agreement with the maintained dense filament response on one symmetric grid, indexing invariants and one invalid-grid case. They do not prove resolved self-fields, arbitrary-grid validity, whole-project reassembly or expert recognition of this development record.
known_limitations: The result is a dense O((N_Z*N_R)^2) matrix and may be costly on large grids.
Current contraction and cell-area factors are caller responsibilities.
Public distribution licensing and SciRel expert recognition remain pending.
The dedicated mirror entry remains limited to uniform, symmetric Z tensor grids; for general irregular coordinates use the actual-coordinate matrix entry in the electromagnetism domain.
